details:
MissionForge: Space Mission Design Game

Project Overview

MissionForge is an interactive educational game designed to introduce the basic concepts of spacecraft mission design. It allows users to explore how different engineering choices affect the feasibility of a space mission through a simple browser-based simulation.

Problem Statement

Designing a space mission requires balancing scientific objectives with engineering constraints such as spacecraft mass, power requirements, communication capabilities, and budget. These concepts can be difficult for beginners to understand without an interactive learning experience.

Our Solution

MissionForge provides a simple, accessible way to explore these trade-offs. Players choose a mission objective and configure different spacecraft systems, including scientific payloads, power systems, communication systems, and launch vehicles. The game evaluates the selected configuration using simplified rules and provides feedback on mission readiness.

Key Features

  • Interactive spacecraft mission configuration.
  • Multiple mission objectives to explore.
  • Selection of scientific instruments and spacecraft systems.
  • Simplified evaluation of mass, power, cost, and science requirements.
  • Mission readiness feedback to encourage experimentation and learning.
  • Browser-based interface that requires no additional software installation.

NASA Space Apps Connection

The project is inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and its focus on space exploration, scientific thinking, and problem-solving. NASA's publicly available educational resources can help users learn more about real space missions and spacecraft technologies.

Technology Used

The prototype is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs in a web browser.

Limitations and Future Improvements

The current version uses illustrative scoring and simplified rules for educational purposes. It is not a professional spacecraft engineering tool. Future improvements could include more realistic mission constraints, additional spacecraft components, and integration of verified NASA datasets.

AI Assistance

AI tools were used to assist with prototyping, code generation, and project documentation. The resulting prototype was reviewed and adapted for the project.
